companies.name: Gentian
companies.description: Nature underpins economies and public services—from productive land and forests to water, flood protection and resilient cities. Yet businesses and governments increasingly need to understand what nature they depend on, how it is changing, and what risks that creates. Over half of the world's GDP depends on this. The problem is that the data needed to answer these questions is often slow, expensive and difficult to obtain. At Gentian, we solve this data problem. Traditional ecological surveys are largely manual, making it difficult and expensive to establish biodiversity baselines, identify nature-related risks, monitor change, or meet regulations such as TNFD and Biodiversity Net Gain. Gentian combines AI with very high-resolution satellite and hyperspectral imagery to automate this work. We can map habitats, individual trees, peatlands, invasive species and other ecological features across very large areas in days - or, in some cases, minutes - turning months of fieldwork into actionable, regulation-ready data. This enables infrastructure, energy, forestry, mining and public-sector organisations to reduce survey costs and delays, identify nature risks earlier, and make better decisions about land. Our technology has already been used by organisations including Shell, Ecolab and major municipalities globally. Sales revenue doubled in 2025 and is on track to double again in 2026. The good news is, we haven't even got going yet.

companies.name: Taylannas Inc.
companies.description: SpeechMED is a multilingual, voice-first patient engagement platform designed to solve one of healthcare’s most persistent and costly failures: patients not understanding medical instructions. Built to serve diverse, aging, and low-literacy populations, SpeechMED delivers personalized, spoken medical guidance in a patient’s preferred language, reinforcing comprehension through reminders, interactive checklists, and feedback loops that fit seamlessly into clinical workflows. Our initial commercial focus is SpeechMED+GI, a colonoscopy preparation module addressing a well-documented pain point across health systems: procedure cancellations caused by poor patient preparation. By replacing written instructions with clear, culturally appropriate audio guidance, SpeechMED+GI improves adherence, reduces staff follow-up time, and protects downstream procedure revenue—without requiring major changes to existing EHR or SMS infrastructure. The platform is AI-ready by design, enabling future conversational and adaptive capabilities while remaining compliant with healthcare privacy and workflow requirements. SpeechMED’s architecture has been validated through grant-funded development with InterSystems and has been purpose-built for enterprise healthcare environments rather than consumer wellness use cases. Traction & Forward Progress SpeechMED has secured accelerator investment and non-dilutive funding, completed successful pilots and quality-improvement initiatives with major academic medical centers and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, and demonstrated early operational ROI through reduced cancellations, improved preparation quality, and measurable staff time savings. The company maintains an active pipeline with large integrated health systems, including continued engagement with the VA—an inherently complex but high-value customer where progress is gated by standardized procurement, compliance, and administration-level transitions that affect all vendors equally. As these processes advance, SpeechMED is focused on converting validated pilots into repeatable contracts, expanding within existing relationships, and extending the platform to additional high-impact procedural and care-navigation use cases. In a market where durability matters more than speed, SpeechMED has remained operational, capital-disciplined, and steadily advancing—positioned to scale as institutional buyers move from experimentation to standardization.

companies.name: Aspect Aerospace
companies.description: At Aspect Aerospace, we are announcing a new piece of revolutionary tech for the space industry. We are leveraging our TRL-9 hardware and software to create a "Single-Board Satellite" -- the entire satellite is a single printed circuit board, able to be mass produced in any PCB assembly house in the US. Each satellite will be 10cm x 10cm to fit inside a CubeSat-sized deployer, with the option to be larger for specialized scenarios. Our goal is to leverage this breakthrough tech to create a space industry in Mobile, Alabama. Leveraging the single-board satellite architecture, we're bringing to market a "constellation in-a-box" -- a whole constellation of 20-100 satellites, deployed from a single CubeSat, for less than the cost of a single CubeSat. Each satellite would cost hundreds of dollars, rather than traditional hundreds of thousands or millions of dollars. With each satellite acting as a node in a constellation, we can do some revolutionary things, each constellation deployed in a single launch -- for instance: - We can do distributed optics, with each satellite hosting a camera, allowing us to do extremely fast revisits, image stacking, 3d stereo optics, etc. While each individual camera is worse than a larger, more traditional camera, by leveraging 20-100 of them, it starts to outperform individual earth observation satellites. - Deployable mesh networks: a large / government-owned and operated satellite could host a cannister of these satellites, ready to go, in the event of adversarial attack or disrupted radio communications -- and rapidly deploy a mesh radio network on-demand. Think of it as a cell network on demand. - Aggregate data collection: dispense a constellation into a space weather storm, patch of high-density neutral particles, etc. to capture data with extreme accuracy. We've licensed tech from a university that can measure both space weather and neutral particle density to sub-meter resolution, allowing us to generate extremely accurate ionosphere maps, for instance. This single-board platform lets us test experimental tech, validate it, license it for market, etc. very rapidly. - Batch testing in space: the bread-and-butter of the company is rapid prototyping and batch testing in space. We can host a component to test, deploy them in-situ across 100 satellites at a lower price point than on-ground testing, and generate 100 hours of space qualification time per real-world hour. You could get 73,000 hours of space qual time in one month, for cheaper than on-ground testing, with a faster turnaround time as these things are mass produced, ready to go. ** We are currently closing our Pre-Seed round, and will update the funding amount section when the deal goes through. This Pre-Seed round will allow us to meet certain technical and market entry milestones to begin leveraging our $5M Seed Round.

companies.name: WellCapped
companies.description: WellCapped enables members to access a shared inventory of high quality wigs and hair extensions. Members are able to access this inventory through three ways: monthly subscription, a-la-carte rentals, and purchasing through our resale program. On average, a wig made with human hair costs $600. This is not including the additional money that consumers spend to have the wig installed. Consumers in the United States are currently spending $1800 annually on human hair extensions and wigs. Our members save money and have more versatility by paying a monthly fee to have a wig shipped to them each month. The wigs are also specially made so that they are easily self-installed by our members, from the comfort of their homes, saving them time and money. We use local contractors to handle the sanitization and restyling of the wigs once the wig is returned. In the future, we want to add an AR component that allows members to virtually try on wigs using an app. Additionally, we use predictive modeling to recommend styles and will eventually scale this model out to products in adjacent categories such as shampoo and conditioner. We are starting with wigs because consumers who wear wigs are typically hyper-consumers of beauty products. This allows us to collect enough data to place our members in hives, which are groups of members with similar preferences. We will use k-means clustering to build the model that will recommend products to our members based on their hive and historical rentals/purchases.

companies.name: Basin Technologies
companies.description: Wind-blown dust is a costly, everyday problem. When land is disturbed by construction, mining, farming, military training ranges, or solar development, dry soil lifts into the air. That dust hurts air quality and public health, cuts visibility on highways, fouls equipment, and lowers the output of solar panels. The usual fixes, such as spraying water, spreading chemical suppressants, or laying gravel, are expensive, need constant reapplication, use a lot of water, or create their own environmental problems. This technology takes a different approach: engineered roughness arrays. These are carefully patterned arrangements of surface elements placed on the ground. By tuning their shape, height, and spacing, the array changes how wind flows right at the surface, slowing it down where it would otherwise pick up loose soil. The result is less dust lifted into the air, with far less water and chemical use than conventional methods. The science behind it comes from research at the Desert Research Institute, part of the Nevada System of Higher Education, building on decades of work studying how wind moves sediment across arid landscapes. Our team is exploring whether this research can solve real problems for the people who deal with dust every day: land managers, contractors, mine operators, defense agencies, and energy developers. We are at the earliest stage of that exploration. The purpose of this work is to talk to potential users, understand where dust control costs them the most, and learn whether an engineered-roughness solution would fit how they actually operate.
